newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus to spend $8 mln on Russian, Ukrainian grain.
newsitem.headline: Belarus to spend $8 mln on Russian, Ukrainian grain.

text.p: The Belarus government has given its central bank permission to buy $8 million on the Minsk Interbank Currency Exchange to purchase grain, most likely from Russia or Ukraine, a top agriculture ministry official said.
The official, who asked not to be named, said the grain would supply flour mills and feed livestock.
Belarus announced plans last year to import 500,000 tonnes of grain during the 1996/97 crop year.
"We plan to import as much grain this year as last year, which is 500,000 tonnes. We will import hard varieties," Deputy Agriculture Minister Ivan Shokolo had told Reuters.
He said Belarus planned to increase sowing areas to achieve a grain harvest of 6.5 million tonnes this year, compared to 5.8 million tonnes in 1996.
The former Soviet republic harvested 5.7 million tonnes and imported one million tonnes of grain in 1995.

Shokolo said the country would increase wheat sowing to 200,000 hectares this year from 55,000 hectares in 1996, adding, "This will let us have a wheat harvest of no less than one million tonnes, against 300,000 tonnes in 1996."
He said winter wheat was doing well and Belarus expected yields of 3.0 tonnes per hectare compared to 2.7 tonnes per hectare from last year's crop.
"Winter grain is going well. It's growing in optimum conditions," he said.
